limitations: No measured frequency for operating-system Worker crashes; browser tests control genuine Worker errors.
Retained derivation assumes job-local selection and scores, independent of catalog-relative statistics.
Retained results derive from the fixed accepted projection; they cannot restore data already absent from it.
Automatic foreground scheduling remains unchanged; a daily-only source configuration may need manual retry for prompt Worker recovery.
Unanimous approval is a phase decision, not a guarantee of a defect-free product.
Constructor failure is injected by the test wrapper; foreground/online/visibility are dispatched events. OS termination, out-of-memory and bfcache restoration are not reproduced.
The existing unit test covers the150s Worker stall guard; this stage does not exercise that timeout in a browser.

Daily-source/legacy timestamp cases are unit-only. Compare values and cross-worker preview generation are checked at1440px; changed-intent preview/selection and staged expiry/saved state also run at320px.

The startup-constructor observer preserves the native fetch promise/Response and proves same-attempt cancellation, with an instrumentation footprint. Only finished/no-error or failed/ERR_ABORTED terminal orderings are accepted; neither implies measured server-resource savings.
Only the nine affected E2E files are this stage's browser evidence; earlier full-suite executions are not counted.
The default fixture checks synthetic server mode and serves dist in production. No separate served-response byte audit is claimed.
Source/control endpoint hashes and the cooperative lock are evidence of this execution; they cannot exclude an external edit-and-restore.
Detailed reporter output, browser/runtime copies and raw logs remain available for final review now and will be deleted after Git preservation.
